name: 江戸切子
desc: 東京都墨田区・江東区を中心に生産されるカットガラス工芸品。1834年（天保5年）、江戸・大伝馬町でビードロ屋を営む加賀屋久兵衛が英国製カットガラスを模してガラスに彫刻を施したのが起源。明治期に英国人指導で西洋式技法が加わり、矢来・魚子（ななこ）・六角籠目などの伝統文様をダイヤモンドホイールで削り出す精緻な技術が確立された。カットの角度が生む光の乱反射と独特の輝きが魅力で、酒器・グラスから現代小物まで幅広く親しまれている。
desc_en: Edo Kiriko is a cut glass craft produced mainly in Sumida Ward and Koto Ward, Tokyo. Said to have originated around 1834 when Edo glassware dealer Kagaya Kyubei engraved glass surfaces with corundum. Characterized by cutting traditional patterns such as yurai (bamboo fence), nanako (fish roe), and hexagonal basket weave using diamond wheels and whetstones, the multi-angle refraction of light creates a unique brilliance. Highly popular domestically and internationally as a representative Tokyo traditional craft, it is enjoyed in diverse products including sake vessels, glasses, and accessories.
techniques: ダイヤモンドホイール切り
features: 伝統文様の精緻な切り込みが生む光の乱反射と美しい輝き

name: 薩摩切子
desc: 鹿児島県鹿児島市で生産される色被せガラスのカット工芸品。幕末の薩摩藩主・島津斉興・斉彬父子が西洋のガラス技術を導入し、1846年頃から生産が始まった。透明ガラスの上に色ガラスを厚く被せ、深くカットすることで「ぼかし」と呼ばれる独特の色グラデーションが生まれる点が最大の特徴。明治維新後に一度途絶えたが、昭和期に現代の職人によって技術が復興された。江戸切子とともに「日本二大切子」として国内外で高く評価されている。
desc_en: Satsuma Kiriko is a cut colored glass craft produced in Kagoshima City, Kagoshima Prefecture. Production began around 1846 when Satsuma Domain lords Shimazu Narioki and Nariakira introduced Western glass technology. Its defining feature is the unique color gradation called 'bokashi' created by thickly applying colored glass over clear glass and then deep-cutting. After disappearing following the Meiji Restoration, the technique was revived by modern craftspeople in the Showa period. Together with Edo Kiriko, it is internationally recognized as one of Japan's 'Two Great Kiriko' glass arts.

name: 京扇子
desc: 京都府京都市で生産される折りたたみ式扇子。平安時代の877年頃に木簡を束ねた「桧扇（ひおうぎ）」が起源とされ、その後紙扇へと発展した。扇骨の加工・地紙の制作・絵付け・貼り加工など複数の専門職人が分業して仕上げる高度な工芸品で、能・狂言・茶道・日本舞踊など日本の伝統芸能に欠かせない必需品として発展した。現代も冠婚葬祭・贈答品から日常の涼取りまで幅広く使われる、日本文化の象徴的な工芸品。
desc_en: Kyo Sensu are folding fans produced in Kyoto City, Kyoto Prefecture. Said to have originated around 877 in the Heian period from 'hiougi,' wooden fans made from bundled wooden tablets, later evolving into paper fans. A sophisticated craft completed through the division of labor among multiple specialist craftspeople covering rib processing, paper creation, painting, and assembly. They developed as indispensable items for traditional Japanese performing arts including Noh, Kyogen, tea ceremony, and Japanese dance. Still widely used today from weddings and ceremonies to gifts and everyday cooling.

name: 江戸扇子
desc: 東京（江戸）で生産される折りたたみ式扇子。京都から伝わった扇子製作の技術が「粋（いき）」な江戸の美意識と融合して独自の様式を確立した。京扇子が多くの職人の分業で作られるのに対し、江戸扇子は一人の職人がすべての工程を担う「江戸の一人仕事」が伝統的な特徴。骨数が少なくシンプルで力強いデザインが多く、落語家・芸人など江戸の庶民文化と深く結びついて発展した。
desc_en: Edo Sensu are folding fans produced in Tokyo (Edo). Fan-making techniques transmitted from Kyoto merged with the 'iki' (stylish refinement) aesthetics of Edo to establish a unique style. While Kyo Sensu is made through the division of labor among many craftspeople, Edo Sensu is traditionally characterized by 'Edo's solo work'—a single craftsperson handling all processes. Featuring fewer ribs and often simple, bold designs, it developed closely intertwined with the popular culture of Edo through rakugo performers and entertainers.
techniques: 一人仕事（全工程単独制作）

name: 京うちわ
desc: 京都府京都市で生産される柄と骨が別体の丸型うちわ。南北朝時代に朝鮮うちわ（朝鮮団扇）が倭寇を通じて西日本にもたらされ、紀州・大和を経て深草に伝わったのが始まりとされる。竹を細かく割いて骨を作り、和紙や絹の面を貼った後に木の柄を後から差し込む「挿し柄（さしえ）」構造が京うちわ独自の特徴。絵師・骨師・貼り師の分業で仕上げる高度な工芸品で、茶道具・夏の装飾品として今も珍重されている。
desc_en: Kyo Uchiwa are round fans with separate handle and ribs, produced in Kyoto City, Kyoto Prefecture. They inherit the style of 'gosho uchiwa' (imperial fan) transmitted from China via the Korean Peninsula during the Nara period. Characterized by the 'sashie' (inserted handle) structure where a wooden handle is inserted after attaching painted washi paper or silk faces onto a finely split bamboo frame. Developed as a sophisticated division-of-labor craft among painters, rib-makers, and pasting specialists for use as summer decorations, cooling tools, and tea ceremony implements.
features: 柄と骨が別体の「挿し柄」構造が京うちわ独自の特徴

name: 丸亀うちわ
desc: 香川県丸亀市で生産される竹製うちわ。現在、日本国内で流通するうちわの約90%が丸亀市産であり、国内最大のうちわ産地として知られる。江戸時代に金刀比羅宮（こんぴらさん）の参拝土産として「渋うちわ」が販売されたことが産地発展の契機となった。竹を割いて骨を作り機械生産と手作業を組み合わせた独自の生産体制で、年間1億本以上を出荷する。夏の風物詩として全国で広く親しまれている。
desc_en: Marugame Uchiwa are bamboo fans produced in Marugame City, Kagawa Prefecture. Currently approximately 90% of fans distributed in Japan are made in Marugame, making it Japan's largest fan production area. The region's development as a production center was triggered by the sale of 'shibu uchiwa' (persimmon-tannin lacquered fans) as souvenirs for Kotohira-gu (Konpira-san) shrine visitors during the Edo period. Using a unique production system combining machine production and hand labor to split bamboo into ribs, it ships more than 100 million fans annually.

name: 房州うちわ
desc: 千葉県館山市・南房総市を中心に生産される竹製丸型うちわ。明治時代中頃から本格的な生産が始まり、房州（南房総）産の女竹（めだけ）を骨に使う点が特徴。1本の竹を丸い柄のまま使い、その先端部分を細く割いて骨を作る「丸柄（まるえ）」製法が独特で、継ぎ目のない一体構造が強度と美しさを兼ね備える。涼感のある丸みを帯びた形と細かい骨格の透け感が夏の風物詩として珍重されている。
desc_en: Boshu Uchiwa are round bamboo fans produced mainly in Tateyama City and Minami Boso City, Chiba Prefecture. Full-scale production began around the mid-Meiji period, distinguished by the use of locally-sourced female bamboo (medake) from Boshu (South Boso) for the ribs. The unique 'marugara' (round handle) technique uses a single bamboo stalk with the round handle intact, finely splitting the tip portion to create ribs—a seamless one-piece construction combining strength and beauty. Prized as a summer seasonal item for its cooling rounded form and the delicate translucency of fine ribs.

name: 甲州水晶貴石細工
desc: 山梨県甲府市を中心とした水晶・貴石加工工芸。約千年前、御嶽昇仙峡の奥地で水晶の原石が発見されたことが起源とされ、江戸時代中期には神官が京都の玉造りに原石を持参して加工させるようになった。その後、江戸時代後期に甲府で研磨技術が確立されると産地として本格的に発展し、明治以降は輸入宝石も扱うジュエリー産業へ拡大。現在も甲府市は国内ジュエリー生産トップシェアを誇る宝石工芸の集積地として知られる。
desc_en: Koshu Crystal Gemstone Work is a crystal and gemstone crafting art centered in Kofu City, Yamanashi Prefecture. Good-quality crystals have been produced in Koshu (Yamanashi) since ancient times, said to have originated when Buddhist monks began making crystal prayer beads around the Kamakura period. During the Edo period, Kofu's crystal craftspeople became known nationwide, and from the Meiji era it developed into a jewelry industry also handling imported gemstones. Today, Kofu City still holds the top domestic share in jewelry production, with concentrated techniques for polishing, carving, and decorating precious stones.

name: 甲州印伝
desc: 山梨県甲府市で生産される鹿革に漆で模様を付けた革工芸品。江戸時代後期には既に財布や巾着の素材として広く親しまれ、滑稽本「東海道中膝栗毛」にも甲州印伝の巾着が登場するほど知られていた。燻した鹿革に型紙で漆を摺り付けて模様を施す技法が独特で、軽くて丈夫な鹿革と漆文様が一体となった財布・バッグ・小物が代表的な製品。現在も甲府市の印伝屋を中心に伝統が守られている。
desc_en: Koshu Inden is a leather craft from Kofu City, Yamanashi Prefecture, featuring deer hide decorated with lacquer patterns. Said to have been founded in the early Edo period by Inden-ya (Uehara Yushichi) in Kofu, it is known as a craft associated with Takeda Shingen's Koshu. The technique is unique: deer hide is smoked and softened, then lacquer patterns are applied using stencils. Representative products include wallets, bags, and small accessories combining the lightweight durability of deer hide with lacquer patterns. The tradition continues today centered on Inden-ya in Kofu.

name: 熊野筆
desc: 広島県安芸郡熊野町で生産される毛筆・化粧筆。江戸時代、農業だけでは生活が難しかった農民が紀州熊野・大和吉野方面へ出稼ぎし、帰路に筆を仕入れて行商したのが縁の始まり。江戸時代後期に広島藩の御用筆司から筆作りを習得した村人が帰郷して技術を広め、産地が形成された。現在は国内の毛筆・化粧筆生産の約80%を占める日本最大の筆産地で、世界の化粧品ブランドからも高く評価される穂作りの技術が受け継がれている。
desc_en: Kumano Fude are calligraphy brushes and makeup brushes produced in Kumano Town, Aki District, Hiroshima Prefecture. Around the Tenpo era (1830-44) at the end of the Edo period, farmers began itinerant brush selling as a side business, acquiring techniques from Nara and Arima to form the production area. Currently the largest brush production area in Japan, accounting for approximately 80% of domestic production of calligraphy brushes, Western brushes, and makeup brushes. The high-quality hair selection and tassel-making techniques are highly regarded by cosmetics brands worldwide, with exports to Europe and China.

name: 豊橋筆
desc: 愛知県豊橋市で生産される毛筆。江戸時代、吉田藩の藩主が京都の職人を御用筆匠として招き、下級武士の副業として筆作りを奨励したのが始まりとされる。明治初年には現代の筆と同じ製法（水筆）が確立され、産地が本格化。熊野（広島）と並ぶ国内二大毛筆産地として知られ、職人が手作業で穂を整える伝統的製法を今も守りながら、練習用から書家向け高級筆まで幅広い書道用筆を生産している。
desc_en: Toyohashi Fude are calligraphy brushes produced in Toyohashi City, Aichi Prefecture. Production is said to have begun around the Bunka era (1804-18) in the Edo period when technicians were invited from Nara, and it is known as one of Japan's two major calligraphy brush production areas alongside Kumano (Hiroshima). The quality of calligraphy brushes, made through careful hair selection and meticulous tassel-making, is highly regarded, and the traditional production method of hand-trimming brush tassels by local craftspeople is still maintained today. The lineup spans from practice brushes for calligraphy classes and schools to premium handmade brushes favored by calligraphers.

name: 赤間硯
desc: 山口県下関市彦島の赤間石を素材とした硯（すずり）。鎌倉時代初めには既に鶴岡八幡宮へ奉納された記録があり、毛利氏（長州藩）の時代には藩主が石山を「御止め山」として管理し、参勤交代の贈り物に用いるほど珍重された。赤紫色のきめ細かい石肌が墨を滑らかに磨り下ろし、発墨の良さで文人・書家に長く愛用されてきた長州藩の名産品。現在も下関の職人が採掘・加工を続けている。
desc_en: Akama Suzuri are inkstones made from Akama stone quarried in Hikoshima, Shimonoseki City, Yamaguchi Prefecture. Akama stone (Akamaga-seki stone), characterized by its reddish-purple hue, has been used for inkstones since around the Nara period. Its fine-grained stone texture grinds ink smoothly with good ink-releasing quality and beautiful ink gliding, long favored by literati and calligraphers as a high-quality inkstone. Counted among Japan's three great inkstones alongside Tankei and Touka, craftspeople continue to quarry and process the stone in Shimonoseki as a representative traditional craft.

奈良時代から文人・書家に愛用されてきた長い歴史

name: 雲州そろばん
desc: 島根県仁多郡奥出雲町（旧仁多町・横田町）で生産される木製そろばん。江戸時代後期、仁多町の大工が広島の職人のそろばんを手本に、地元のカシ・ウメ・ススタケを使って作り始めたのが起源。横田町の職人が珠を削る手回しろくろを完成させたことで生産が急増し、「そろばんといえば雲州」と全国に知られる産地となった。現在は国内のそろばん生産の約70%を占める日本最大の産地で、精密な手作りの技術が今も受け継がれている。
desc_en: Unshu Soroban are wooden abacuses produced in Okuizumo Town, Nita District, Shimane Prefecture. Around the mid-Edo period, production began as a side business for farmers, developing into a production area utilizing the characteristics of the mountain region's abundant quality wood and bamboo. Currently the largest abacus production area in Japan, accounting for approximately 70% of domestic production, with the precise handcrafting method of finishing all wooden frames, beams, and beads by hand still being maintained. Even in modern times with widespread ICT education, there is continued strong demand as a tool for mental arithmetic and mathematics education, with high regard as a traditional craft.

Made by forming cotton into a round core and then meticulously wrapping colorful silk and cotton threads in intricate geometric patterns. Developed in the castle town of the Takamatsu Domain during the Edo period as New Year's good luck charms and toys for girls, production spread among craftspeople and ordinary households. Today they are enjoyed as New Year decorations, interior accessories, and gifts, with temari classes and hands-on experiences actively held throughout the region.

Made by repeatedly coating an inner core of rush grass and Japanese paper with wood wax extracted from the fruits of hazenoki and urushi trees. They have characteristics of a large flickering flame, little soot, and long burning time. Developed as a uniquely Japanese candle culture indispensable for Buddhist ceremonies, Shinto rituals, and tea ceremony, with Kyoto, Aichi (Isshiki), Shiga, and Toyama known as major production areas.

desc_en: Bekko Zaiku is decorative crafts made from hawksbill sea turtle shell, produced mainly in Taito Ward (around Asakusa and Ueno), Tokyo. Techniques transmitted from Nagasaki around the mid-Edo period developed in Edo/Tokyo, with hair ornaments (kanzashi), brooches, eyeglass frames, and obi clasps as representative products. The distinctive technique involves heating the hawksbill shell in hot water or flame to soften it, then pressing it into molds for shaping and joining. Currently the number of craftspeople and production volume are declining due to difficulty sourcing materials under CITES (Washington Convention) commercial trade restrictions, though production with existing materials and development of alternative materials continue.

desc_en: Awa Ningyo Joruri Puppets are craft puppets used in 'Awa Ningyo Joruri,' a traditional performing art of Tokushima Prefecture. From the early Edo period, ningyo joruri (puppet theater) took root in the farming villages of Tokushima (Awa), developing a unique Awa style influenced by Osaka's Bunraku. The puppets have sophisticated structures operated by the main puppeteer (or three puppeteers) moving the torso, head, and limbs, with expressively carved heads, intricately embroidered costumes, and precision-engineered limb mechanisms showcasing the pinnacle of puppet-maker craftsmanship. Still performed at rural kabuki and Obon festivals, they are iconic craft objects of Tokushima's proud traditional performing arts.

name: 岐阜提灯
desc: 岐阜県岐阜市で生産される長良川和紙と竹を使った伝統的な提灯。江戸時代中期頃から岐阜の豊富な竹・和紙を活かした提灯制作が始まり、盆提灯の主要産地として発展した。細い竹ひごを螺旋状に巻いた骨組みに薄い美濃和紙を貼り、絵師が草花・風景・家紋などを描き入れる。和紙を通した柔らかく幻想的な灯りは日本の夏の風物詩で、岐阜は国内盆提灯生産の主要産地として全国に出荷している。
desc_en: Gifu Chochin are traditional lanterns produced in Gifu City, Gifu Prefecture, using Nagara River washi paper and bamboo. Around the mid-Edo period, lantern production began utilizing Gifu's abundant bamboo and washi paper, developing into a major production area for Obon lanterns. Thin bamboo strips are wound in a spiral frame, covered with thin Mino washi paper, onto which painters add flowers, landscapes, and family crests. The soft, fantastical light through the washi paper is a summer seasonal feature in Japan, and Gifu ships nationwide as a major domestic producer of Obon lanterns.

desc_en: Edo Glass is blown glasswork that developed in Tokyo (Edo) from the late Edo period. From the end of the Edo period through the Meiji era, Western glass techniques merged with Japanese craftsmanship, producing pieces through 'chubuki' (free blowing) where glass is blown with a blowpipe, and 'kataguki' (mold blowing). Unlike Edo Kiriko, which often features cut decoration, Edo Glass is characterized by the simple, warm forms of blown glass. Representative items include goldfish bowls, sake bottles (tokkuri), and sake cups (guinomi), still cherished today as crafts breathed into life by Tokyo artisans.

name: 越後上布
desc: 新潟県南魚沼市・魚沼市を中心に生産される麻織物の最高峰。奈良時代には越後国の特産品として朝廷への献上品となっていたほどの長い歴史を持つ。苧麻（ちょま）の細い繊維を指先で手績みした極細の糸で手機（てばた）により織られ、積雪を利用した「雪さらし」で白く漂白する工程が特徴的。2009年にはユネスコ無形文化遺産に「越後上布・小千谷縮布」として登録され、日本麻織物の最高峰として国際的に評価されている。
desc_en: Echigo Jofu is the pinnacle of linen textiles produced mainly in Minamiuonuma City and Uonuma City, Niigata Prefecture. It has a long history, having been offered as tribute to the imperial court as a specialty of Echigo Province since the Nara period. It is woven on handlooms using ultrafine threads spun by hand from the thin fibers of ramie (choma), with the characteristic process of bleaching white using 'yuki sarashi' (snow bleaching) by spreading the fabric on snow. In 2009, it was registered as a UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage as 'Echigo Jofu and Ojiya Chijimi Fabrics,' internationally recognized as the pinnacle of Japanese linen weaving.

desc: 三重県伊賀市で生産される絹糸の組紐（くみひも）。奈良時代から仏具・装束の飾り紐として発展し、江戸時代には帯締め・羽織紐など和装の小物として需要が拡大した。台組（だいぐみ）と呼ばれる丸台・角台・高台などの専用道具で、複数の糸を規則的に組み上げる技法が特徴。現代は和装小物にとどまらず、ハンドバッグの持ち手・ブレスレット・ネクタイなど現代ファッション小物にも展開。映画「君の名は。」（2016年）のモチーフとして世界的に注目された。
desc_en: Iga Kumihimo are braided silk cords produced in Iga City, Mie Prefecture. Developed from the Nara period as decorative cords for Buddhist implements and imperial robes, demand expanded during the Edo period for Japanese clothing accessories such as obi clasps and haori ties. The technique is characterized by the use of specialized tools called 'daigumi' such as marudai (round stand), kakudai (square stand), and takadai (high stand) to systematically braid multiple threads together. Today, production extends beyond Japanese clothing accessories to modern fashion items including handbag handles, bracelets, and neckties. Gained worldwide attention as the motif of the film 'Your Name' (2016).

desc_en: Suruga Hinagu are small accessories and furnishings for hinaningyo (traditional dolls for Girls' Day) produced in Shizuoka City (formerly Suruga Province), Shizuoka Prefecture. At the beginning of the Edo period, when Tokugawa Ieyasu built Sunpu Castle, craftspeople gathered from across Japan and diverse craft techniques took root in Shizuoka, forming the foundation of the production area. Characterized by the intricate lacquerwork, bamboo crafts, embroidery, and metal fittings on the miniature furnishings for the hinaningyo display (shrine cabinets, palanquins, chests of drawers, large trunks, dressing tables, etc.), it is known as a production area for accessories and furnishings rather than the dolls themselves. desc: 兵庫県小野市で生産されるそろばん。安土桃山時代に豊臣秀吉の三木城攻略の折、大津に逃れた住民がそろばんの技法を習得して帰郷し、製造を始めたのが起源とされる。雲州そろばん（島根）と並ぶ国内二大そろばん産地の一つで、現代でも国産そろばんの大半を生産している。珠をひとつひとつ手作業で仕上げる精密な工程が特徴で、近年はそろばん学習の再評価とともに需要も回復しつつある。
desc_en: Banshu Soroban are abacuses produced in Ono City, Hyogo Prefecture. One of Japan's two major abacus production areas alongside Unshu Soroban (Shimane Prefecture), it remains a leading production center producing the majority of domestically made abacuses today. Production began centered in Ono City from the mid-Edo period, characterized by the precise process of individually hand-finishing each one-unit and five-unit bead and a commitment to ease of use. In recent years, demand has recovered along with a reassessment of abacus learning, and it is attracting attention as a traditional craft supporting Japan's culture of mental arithmetic.

desc: 青森県津軽地方に伝わる刺し子の一種。江戸時代から農村女性が麻布に白い木綿糸でびっしりと刺していく独特の刺繍技法で、防寒・補強の実用性と幾何学的な美しさを兼ね備える。「こぎん」の語源は「小巾（こはば）」で、もとは農作業着（こぎん着）の補強として発展した。水玉・十字・斜め格子などの幾何学文様が特徴で、雪深い津軽の長い冬の手仕事として女性たちが受け継いできた東北を代表する刺し子工芸。
desc_en: Tsugaru Kogin Zashi is a type of sashiko embroidery from the Tsugaru region of Aomori Prefecture. Since the Edo period, rural women have used a distinctive embroidery technique of closely stitching white cotton thread onto linen cloth, combining the practicality of cold protection and reinforcement with geometric beauty. The word 'kogin' derives from 'kohaba' (small width), originally developing as reinforcement for farm work clothing (kogin clothing). Characterized by geometric patterns such as polka dots, crosses, and diagonal lattice, it has been passed down by women as the winter handiwork of snowy Tsugaru, representing Tohoku's sashiko craft tradition.

name: 那智黒石工芸品
desc: 三重県熊野市で産出・加工される那智黒石を使った工芸品。熊野の那智黒石は粘板岩の一種で、きめが細かく研磨すると漆黒の光沢が生まれることが特徴。室町時代から碁石・硯・置物などに加工されてきた歴史を持ち、特に日本の碁石の大部分は那智黒石から作られてきた。熊野三山参詣との結びつきから全国に知られ、囲碁文化を支えてきた重要な石材産地として今日まで受け継がれている。
desc_en: Nachiguro Ishi Kogeihin are craft objects produced using nachiguro stone quarried and processed in Kumano City, Mie Prefecture. Nachiguro stone from Kumano is a type of slate (phylite), characterized by its fine grain that produces a jet-black luster when polished. It has a history of being processed into go pieces, inkstones, and figurines since the Muromachi period, and most of Japan's go pieces have traditionally been made from nachiguro stone. Known throughout Japan through its connection with the pilgrimage to the Kumano Sanzan shrines, it continues to be passed down today as an important stone material production area supporting go culture.
features: 漆黒の光沢が美しい那智黒石は日本の碁石の主要原材料産地
室町時代から碁石・硯・置物に加工される熊野の伝統石工芸
熊野三山参詣文化と結びついた全国に知られる三重の石材産地

name: 甲州手彫印章
desc: 山梨県甲府市で生産される手彫り印章（はんこ・印鑑）。甲州水晶の加工技術が根付いた甲府の職人技術が印章彫刻にも展開され、江戸時代後期から産地として発展してきた。職人が一点一点手彫りで文字・文様を彫る細密な技術と、水晶・黒水牛・柘植など多様な素材使いが特徴の高級手彫り印章産地として全国に知られる。機械彫りとは一線を画す手彫りの温かみと精緻さが、官公庁・法人・個人の重要印として根強い需要を支えている。
desc_en: Koshu Tebori Insho are hand-carved seals (hanko/inkan) produced in Kofu City, Yamanashi Prefecture. The craftsmen's skills rooted in the processing of Koshu crystal were also applied to seal carving, developing as a production area from the late Edo period. Known nationwide as a high-quality hand-carved seal production area, characterized by intricate techniques of hand-carving characters and patterns one by one, and the use of diverse materials including crystal, black water buffalo horn, and boxwood. The warmth and precision of hand carving that sets it apart from machine carving continues to support steady demand for important seals used by government offices, corporations, and individuals.
features: 甲州水晶の加工技術から発展した甲府の精緻な手彫り印章産地
水晶・黒水牛・柘植など多様な高級素材に手彫りで文字を刻む技術
機械彫りとは異なる温かみと精緻さが重要印章として根強く愛用される

name: 京表具
desc: 京都で制作される掛け軸・屏風・襖・巻物などの表具（表装）工芸。平安時代から宮廷・寺院の絵画・書を保護・展示するための表装技術として発展し、薄美濃紙・金箔・錦裂などの高級素材を組み合わせた格調ある仕立てが特徴。文化財保存の要でもある京表具師の技術は国内外の美術品修復にも活用される。古都京都の文化的土壌で磨かれた表具の美は、和の精神と職人技の粋を体現する工芸として現代も高い評価を受ける。
desc_en: Kyo Hyogu is the craft of mounting and framing—hanging scrolls, folding screens, sliding doors, and scrolls—produced in Kyoto. Developed from the Heian period as a technique for protecting and displaying paintings and calligraphy for the imperial court and temples, it features dignified finishing combining premium materials such as thin Mino paper, gold leaf, and brocade. The skills of Kyoto mounting craftspeople, also essential for cultural property conservation, are applied to art restoration domestically and internationally. The beauty of mounting refined in the cultural soil of ancient Kyoto continues to receive high acclaim today as a craft embodying the spirit of Japanese aesthetics and the pinnacle of craftsmen's skills.
techniques: 裂地（きれじ）選定・縫製
